response.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT f.rating AS rating, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), shares AS (SELECT rating, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM counts), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS a FROM shares) SELECT COUNT(*) AS rating_count, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.a) AS avg_excess FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.a

assumptions.assumption: Each rental row counts as one rental transaction; inner joins to inventory and film drop rentals without a matching copy or film.
The average share across ratings is the unweighted mean of per-rating shares over the ratings present after the joins (equal to 1/number of ratings).
